name: Wilsons Promontory National Park
note: National park: southernmost mainland national park, rainforest, beaches and wildlife; Tidal River is its visitor hub. Parks Victoria lists its top places (Tidal River, day walks, Squeaky Beach, Southern Circuit, Lightstation).

name: Tidal River
note: Visitor hub inside the national park: campground, accommodation, store and the start of most day walks. Base for the park, not a sight in itself.

name: Squeaky Beach
note: Beach in Wilsons Promontory National Park: white squeaky sand, short walk from the car park; Parks Victoria top place.

name: Norman Beach
note: Beach at Tidal River inside Wilsons Promontory National Park: swimming and snorkelling, a few minutes' walk from the campground.

name: Picnic Bay
note: Beach in Wilsons Promontory National Park, on the Norman, Squeaky, Picnic and Whisky Bay walk.

name: Whisky Bay
note: Beach at the eastern end of Wilsons Promontory National Park, reached on the Three Bays and beach walks.

name: Mount Oberon
note: Granite summit walk (hike) in Wilsons Promontory National Park, about 6.8 km return from Telegraph Saddle with 360-degree views; Parks Victoria top place.

name: Mount Bishop
note: Summit walk (hike) in Wilsons Promontory National Park from Lilly Pilly Gully, 7.4 km return, with views over the west coast and offshore islands. Wikipedia title ambiguous, so no article used.

name: Lilly Pilly Gully
note: Rainforest gully and nature walk (boardwalk) in Wilsons Promontory National Park, with circuit and link walks; a family-friendly walk.

name: Tongue Point
note: Granite headland at the end of the Darby River to Tongue Point walk in Wilsons Promontory National Park; coastal walk (hike) destination.

name: Sparkes Lookout
note: Lookout (viewpoint) on the Darby Saddle to Tongue Point track in Wilsons Promontory National Park, views to Rodondo Island and Shallow Inlet; a side track of the walk.

name: Vereker Outlook
note: Lookout (viewpoint) in the northern area of Wilsons Promontory National Park with a wide view over the park; short walk from the north-end track.

name: Wilsons Promontory Lightstation
note: Historic lighthouse and cottages at South East Point, the southernmost settlement on mainland Australia; reached on foot on the Southern Prom Circuit.

name: Sealers Cove
note: Remote beach and campsite on the eastern side of Wilsons Promontory, reached by the Southern Prom Circuit hike; boardwalk reopened 2026 per Parks Victoria news.

name: Cleft Island (Skull Rock)
note: Granite island with a cave through it, known as Skull Rock, reached by boat tour from Port Welshpool area; a natural rock feature in Wilsons Promontory.

name: Fairy Cove
note: Secluded cove reached by a side track from the Darby River to Tongue Point walk in Wilsons Promontory National Park.

name: Big Drift
note: Sand dunes (walk) in the Wilsons Promontory area used for sandboarding; mentioned on a Wikipedia photo caption only, no visitor listing found.

name: Croajingolong National Park
note: National park on the far-east coast: inlets, giant dunes, wilderness coast; a UNESCO biosphere reserve; Parks Victoria lists its walks and camping.

name: Point Hicks Lightstation
note: Historic lighthouse and the coastal lookout where Captain Cook is believed to have first landed in Victoria, in Croajingolong National Park.

name: Wilderness Coast Walk
note: Multi-day coastal walk (hike) from Sydenham Inlet to Wonboyn in NSW, through Croajingolong National Park; Parks Victoria lists it as a featured walk.

name: Thurra River Sand Dunes
note: Giant sand dunes beside Thurra River in Croajingolong National Park, with a campground nearby; Wikivoyage lists them under the park's See section.

name: Rame Head
note: Headland (viewpoint) on the Croajingolong coast, listed in Wikivoyage's park See section.

name: Mount Everard
note: Walk to a summit (hike) in Croajingolong National Park, a short walk from the park's heathland; Parks Victoria lists it among the shorter walks.

name: Fly Cove Walk
note: Coastal walk (track) from Wingan Inlet Campground to Fly Cove, where fur seals rest on rocky islets; Parks Victoria listed.

name: Mallacoota
note: Coastal town on Mallacoota Inlet, base for the far-east coast, inlet boating and the Wilderness Coast; the town is a visitor base.

name: Captain Stephenson's Point
note: Headland lookout (viewpoint) at Mallacoota, listed in Wikivoyage's See section for the town.

name: Bastion Point
note: Lookout (viewpoint) above Mallacoota Inlet, recommended by Visit East Gippsland.

name: Genoa Falls
note: Waterfall a short walk from the roadside about 25 km north-west of Mallacoota, on the Genoa River; in East Gippsland.

name: Genoa Peak
note: Summit walk (hike) near Genoa, a more demanding climb with ladders near the top; listed in the Mallacoota-Genoa itinerary.

name: Gabo Island Lightstation
note: Historic island lightstation reached by boat from Mallacoota; the island is a wildlife and lighthouse visit.

name: Pebbly Beach
note: Quiet beach near Mallacoota, recommended by Visit East Gippsland.

name: Quarry Beach
note: Beach at Mallacoota with rock formations, recommended by Visit East Gippsland.

name: WWII Bunker Museum
note: Museum (museum) in a WWII bunker at Mallacoota, open on Tuesdays; a small local museum.

name: Sydenham Inlet
note: Inlet (natural feature) in Croajingolong National Park at the start of the Wilderness Coast Walk; paddling and boating.

name: Snowy River National Park
note: National park along the Snowy River's gorges and old-growth forest; Parks Victoria lists its river scenery and wildlife.

name: Tulloch Ard Gorge
note: Deep gorge where the Snowy River cuts through Snowy River National Park; Parks Victoria describes it as a feature of the park.

name: Orbost
note: Town on the Snowy River and Princes Highway, a service and visitor-information base for the Snowy River country.

name: Buchan Caves
note: Limestone caves with guided tours, near the village of Buchan; a visitor attraction with guided cave tours.

name: Errinundra National Park
note: Forest national park in East Gippsland with rainforest, camping and walks; Parks Victoria lists its boardwalk, lookout and walking tracks.

name: Errinundra Rainforest Boardwalk
note: Boardwalk through cool temperate rainforest in Errinundra National Park; a short walk from the park's facilities.

name: Ocean View Lookout
note: Lookout (viewpoint) in Errinundra National Park; listed by Parks Victoria among the park's sites.

name: Mount Ellery Walk
note: Walking track (hike) to Mount Ellery in Errinundra National Park; listed by Parks Victoria.

name: Coopracambra National Park
note: Remote wilderness national park on the Far East Gippsland border with NSW; bushwalking and camping.

name: Cape Conran Coastal Park
note: Coastal park on the Wilderness Coast with beaches, camping and whale watching (May to October); Parks Victoria lists it.

name: East Cape Boardwalk
note: Boardwalk with interpretive signs on the headland at Cape Conran Coastal Park; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Lind National Park
note: Small coastal national park near Cann River with a coastal walk and camping; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Alfred National Park
note: Forest national park near Orbost with walking tracks; no visitor listing fetched yet.

name: Gippsland Lakes
note: Largest inland waterway system in Australia: lakes, boating, fishing and sailing, the region's main water draw.

name: Gippsland Lakes Coastal Park
note: Coastal park along Ninety Mile Beach from Seaspray to Lakes Entrance, with wetlands, kayaking and free camping; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Ninety Mile Beach
note: Long surf beach (about 90 miles) from Lakes Entrance to Seaspray, a surf fishing and beach-driving coast.

name: Lakes Entrance
note: Coastal resort town at the mouth of the Gippsland Lakes, base for the lakes, Ninety Mile Beach and Buchan Caves.

name: Griffith's Shell Museum
note: Museum of seashells and marine curios in Lakes Entrance, with a giant octopus on the roof; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Lake Tyers Beach
note: Beach by the Lake Tyers inlet near Lakes Entrance; no Wikipedia article of its own (the lake article redirects to a mission); counted source not confirmed.

name: Paynesville
note: Lakeside boating town on the Gippsland Lakes, base for sailing, fishing and lake cruises; a small town.

name: Metung
note: Small village on the Gippsland Lakes at Bancroft Bay, a boating and sailing village.

name: Bairnsdale
note: Regional town and gateway to the Gippsland Lakes and East Gippsland; Wikivoyage's regional hub listing.

name: Mitchell River and Botanic Gardens
note: Riverside park with gardens, a suspension footbridge and a walk along the Mitchell River in Bairnsdale.

name: Mitchell River National Park
note: Gorge national park on the Mitchell River with the Den of Nargun loop walk and rapids; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Den of Nargun
note: Rainforest gully and cave (natural feature) in Mitchell River National Park, a loop walk with a picnic area; Parks Victoria describes it.

name: Sale
note: Regional town and service hub of Central Gippsland; Wikivoyage's regional listing for Sale.

name: Sale Swing Bridge
note: Historic 1883 swing bridge over the Thomson River that rotates 360 degrees, Victoria's first movable bridge; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Gippsland Art Gallery
note: Regional art gallery in the Port of Sale precinct with exhibitions on local art and history; free entry, Wikivoyage listed.

name: Traralgon Railway Reservoir Conservation Reserve
note: Reserve (nature) around the Traralgon railway reservoir with walking paths; a local reserve in Traralgon listed on Wikivoyage.

name: Traralgon
note: Largest town in the Latrobe Valley, a regional service hub on the Princes Highway.

name: Morwell National Park
note: Forest national park near Morwell with walking tracks and a waterfall; no visitor listing fetched yet.

name: Stratford Knob Reserve
note: Reserve (nature) of walking paths on the Avon River outside Stratford, a traditional Gunaikurnai meeting place.

name: Gippsland Plains Rail Trail
note: Rail trail (track) from Traralgon to Stratford for walking and cycling; Wikivoyage names its eastern end at Apex Park.

name: Walhalla
note: Preserved gold-mining town in a steep valley, a heritage village with historic buildings and a goldfields walk; Visit Gippsland lists it as a West Gippsland destination.

name: Walhalla Goldfields Railway
note: Heritage railway (ride) running from Walhalla; the ride is the means to the town, so it is a vehicle, not a spot. Listed so the judge can decide.

name: Tarra-Bulga National Park
note: Cool temperate rainforest national park with giant mountain ash, fern gullies and myrtle beeches; Parks Victoria's top park for walks.

name: Corrigan's Suspension Bridge
note: Suspension footbridge through the rainforest canopy in Tarra-Bulga National Park, a walk (track) with views of the fern gully.

name: Grand Ridge Road
note: Unsealed scenic drive (road) through the Strzelecki Ranges' remnant rainforest, a drive rather than a place; Wikivoyage recommends it for lyrebirds and koalas.

name: Baw Baw National Park
note: Alpine plateau national park with snowgum forests, granite tors, snowshoe trails and wildflowers; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Mushroom Rocks
note: Maze of giant granite tors (natural feature) on the Baw Baw Plateau, reached on a walk from the plateau; Parks Victoria names it.

name: Mount Baw Baw
note: Small alpine ski resort on the Baw Baw Plateau, snow sports in winter and walking and wildflowers in spring; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Tooronga Falls
note: Waterfall near Noojee with a camping area and short walking circuits; Wikivoyage lists it in South Gippsland.

name: Mount Erica
note: Mountain (peak) in the Baw Baw ranges near Erica, with walking tracks; a peak, no visitor listing fetched yet.

name: Cape Liptrap Coastal Park
note: Coastal park on the South Gippsland coast with cliffs, beaches and a lighthouse at Cape Liptrap; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Inverloch
note: Coastal town on Bass Strait with surf beaches and the Bunurong coast; a visitor town for beaches and surfing.

name: Bunurong Marine National Park
note: Marine national park on the South Gippsland coast near Inverloch, rock platforms and reefs; no visitor listing fetched yet.

name: Port Albert
note: Historic 19th-century port village on Corner Inlet with heritage buildings and a pier; a small heritage town.

name: Foster Dam
note: Dam viewing area near Foster, a small lookout listed by Wikivoyage.

name: Warragul
note: Town in West Gippsland, base for the Baw Baw region and rail trail; regional service town.

name: Civic Park Warragul
note: Gardens and picnic park in Warragul's town centre, listed by Wikivoyage.

name: Wild Dog Winery
note: Winery (venue) near Warragul with cellar door tastings; Wikivoyage lists it.

name: Leongatha
note: Town in South Gippsland, centre of the local region and base for the Great Southern Rail Trail.

name: Lennie Gwyther Statue
note: Bronze statue (monument) in Leongatha of a boy who rode 1000 km on horseback to the Sydney Harbour Bridge opening in 1932; a quirky roadside landmark.

name: Coal Creek Community Park and Museum
note: Recreated 1890s mining village and museum at Korumburra; an open-air heritage park visitors walk around.

name: Great Southern Rail Trail
note: Rail trail (track) from Leongatha to Welshpool for walking and cycling; Visit Gippsland lists rail trails.

name: Old Gippstown
note: Open-air heritage village museum at Moe with restored buildings from across Gippsland; a visitor museum.

name: Wonthaggi State Coal Mine
note: Heritage coal-mine museum at Wonthaggi with guided tours of the mine; a heritage site.

name: Agnes Falls
note: Waterfall near Walhalla in the Gippsland hills, reached by a short walk; search results mention it among Gippsland highlights.

name: Bunyip State Park
note: Forested state park in West Gippsland with walking tracks and waterfalls; Parks Victoria lists it.

name: Nooramunga Marine and Coastal Park
note: Coastal and marine park in Corner Inlet area of Gippsland, with boating, fishing and wetlands; Parks Victoria lists it.
